S-creatinin (serum creatinine) is a specific laboratory parameter used to assess renal function in patients with [[atrieflimren]] who are treated with [[doac|DOAC]] (Direct Oral Anticoagulants). Within the Danish national quality program for atrial fibrillation, S-creatinin is the primary biomarker tracked by [[indikator-4b|Indikator 4b]], which monitors the safety and evidence-based follow-up of anticoagulation therapy [^src4]. 

To fulfill the requirements of [[indikator-4b|Indikator 4b]], prevalent patients on DOAC therapy must have at least one measurement of S-creatinin recorded annually [^src4]. The national quality standard mandates that ≥ 95% of these patients receive this annual renal function monitoring [^src1]. Recent reports from the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) highlight that while S-creatinin (along with P-creatinin) is central to this safety indicator, there is notable geographic variation in the fulfillment of the ≥ 95% target across different regions and health clusters [^src3]. This underscores the need for targeted quality improvement and better integration of laboratory data across healthcare sectors to ensure patient safety during long-term DOAC treatment [^src3].
